item.title: Append-Only as Proof: A Formal Account of Governance Sovereignty in AI Audit Systems
item.description:
Authors: Reuben Bowlby

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: We formalize the distinction between records (mutable documentation of claims) and proofs (tamper-evident, independently observable witnesses) in AI audit systems. We identify five necessary invariants — the KRINEIA invariants — for an audit log to constitute a governance proof: append-only, no reward-path self-reference, minimal operators, external analysis only, and trust-root separation. We prove each is individually necessary and all five are jointly sufficient. We show that all current major AI governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act Article 18, ISO 42001 clause 9.1) specify records rather than proofs and are therefore structurally incapable of distinguishing genuine governance from governance theater. We instantiate the framework in a production multi-agent system with 42,961+ audit bus entries and demonstrate detection of the A4 phantom delivery probe class.
